definition_en: to plant seeds in the ground or to spread an idea or feeling
core_image: 农人弯着腰，把种子一把把撒进翻好的土里
scene: 农民在春天播种小麦。The farmer sows wheat in spring.
sceneCN: 这里 sow 是「播种」（第 1 个义项）；句意：农民在春天播种小麦。

senses.title: To plant seeds
senses.definition: to put seeds in the ground so they can grow
senses.definitionCN: 把种子放进土里使其生长
senses.example: The farmer sows wheat in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 农民在春天播种小麦。
senses.why: This is the central farming sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最核心的农耕含义。

senses.title: To seed a field
senses.definition: to plant a field or piece of land with seeds
senses.definitionCN: 在田地或土地上播种
senses.example: They sowed the field with barley.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在田里种了大麦。
senses.why: The object can be the seed or the ground.
senses.whyCN: 宾语可以是种子，也可以是土地。

senses.title: To spread an idea
senses.definition: to cause an idea or feeling to begin and spread
senses.definitionCN: 使某种想法或情感产生并传播
senses.example: The speech sowed doubt in their minds.
senses.exampleCN: 这番话在他们心中播下了疑虑。
senses.why: Ideas grow like seeds once they are planted.
senses.whyCN: 想法一旦种下，就像种子一样生长。

intro.en: Sow is an old farming verb shared across Germanic languages.

definition_en: an empty area, the region beyond the earth, or a gap between things

definition_zh: 航天器；宇宙飞船；探测器
definition_en: a vehicle designed to travel in space, crewed or unmanned
core_image: 银白色的航天器在地球弧线之上缓缓展开太阳能板
scene: 这艘航天器成功进入了轨道。The spacecraft entered orbit successfully.

senses.title: A space vehicle

core.en: The reach between two outstretched points.

branches.en: An arch joins two banks.

branches.en: Distance and time are both measured by reach.
branches.cn: 距离与时间，都用「触及」来丈量。

definition_en: to give time or money, to save, to forgive, or kept as extra
core_image: 柜子里放着一把备用钥匙，静静等着需要它的那天
scene: 你能抽出几分钟吗？Can you spare a few minutes?
sceneCN: 这里 spare 是「抽出」（第 1 个义项）；句意：你能抽出几分钟吗？

senses.title: To give time or resources
senses.definition: to be able to give time, money, or effort to someone
senses.definitionCN: 能够把时间、金钱或精力分给别人
senses.example: Can you spare a few minutes?
senses.exampleCN: 你能抽出几分钟吗？
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of making room for others.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常表示为他人腾出余地的含义。

senses.title: To forgive
senses.definition: to choose not to harm or punish someone
senses.definitionCN: 选择不伤害或惩罚某人
senses.example: The king spared the prisoner.
senses.exampleCN: 国王饶了那个囚犯。
senses.why: To spare is to hold back the blow.
senses.whyCN: 饶恕，就是把打击收住。

senses.title: Kept as extra
senses.definition: kept in addition in case it is needed
senses.definitionCN: 额外保留以备需要
senses.example: We keep a spare key under the mat.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在垫子下放了一把备用钥匙。
senses.why: What is set aside is being spared for later.
senses.whyCN: 被留出来的东西，就是为以后省下的。

intro.en: Spare first meant to hold back from harming.
intro.cn: spare 最初意为克制不去伤害。

items.en: Sparian meant to refrain from harming or using.
items.cn: sparian 意为不伤害或不使用。

items.en: The form became spare and kept mercy.
items.cn: 词形变为 spare，保留宽恕之义。

items.en: It came to mean to save or set aside.
items.cn: 它开始表示节省或留出。

items.en: The adjective named what is kept extra.
items.cn: 形容词指额外保留的东西。

items.en: Phrases like spare time fixed the modern uses.
items.cn: spare time 等短语固定了现代用法。

note.en: Spare is compared with look-alike words and words for saving.
note.cn: 把 spare 与形近词以及表示节省、宽恕的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: To spare is to loosen your hold on something for someone else.
normalIntro.cn: spare 是为别人放松对某物的握持。

normal.en: Can you spare a few minutes?

normal.en: The king spared the prisoner.

normal.en: We keep a spare key under the mat.

normal.en: He spares no effort in his work.
normal.cn: 他在工作中不遗余力。

normal.en: Spare a thought for those who are cold.
normal.cn: 体谅一下那些受冻的人。

abstract.en: Spare is a word that makes room for mercy.
abstract.cn: spare 是一个为宽恕腾出空间的词。

abstract.en: What we spare, we still care for.
abstract.cn: 我们饶过的东西，说明我们仍在意。

abstract.en: A spare minute is a gift with no wrapping.
abstract.cn: 空出的一分钟，是一份没有包装的礼物。

examples.en: We keep a spare key under the mat.

root: 来自古英语 sparian（不伤害、不使用），核心义为克制与保留，后分化为抽出、饶恕与备用。

sensesIntro.en: Spare means to give time or resources, to forgive, or to keep something extra.
sensesIntro.cn: spare 指抽出时间或资源、饶恕他人，或保留备用的东西。

core.en: Holding back what could be used or given.
core.cn: 对本可使用或给予之物的克制。

branches.en: A busy person pauses to listen.
branches.cn: 忙碌的人停下来倾听。

branches.en: A hand is raised to strike but stops.
branches.cn: 举起来要打的手停住了。

branches.en: A spare key waits under a mat.
branches.cn: 一把备用钥匙等在垫子下。

branches.en: Giving time and giving mercy are both letting go.
branches.cn: 给出时间与给出宽恕，都是放手。

branches.en: What is spared is kept for a future need.
branches.cn: 被饶过或保留的，是留给未来需要的。

intro.en: Spare forms a verb paradigm and two derived modifiers.
intro.cn: spare 构成动词变化形式和两个派生修饰词。

definition_zh: 火花；引发；一丝（希望或兴趣）
definition_en: a small burning particle, to cause something to start, or a trace of a feeling
core_image: 营火中迸出一点橙红的火星，落在干燥的草地上
scene: 火星从营火中迸溅出来。A spark flew from the campfire.
sceneCN: 这里 spark 是「火花」（第 1 个义项）；句意：火星从营火中迸溅出来。

senses.title: A small flame
senses.definition: a tiny piece of burning material flying from a fire
senses.definitionCN: 从火中飞出的细小燃烧颗粒
senses.example: A spark flew from the campfire.
senses.exampleCN: 火星从营火中迸溅出来。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most physical sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老、最具体的含义。

senses.title: To set off
senses.definition: to cause something such as an argument or change to begin
senses.definitionCN: 使争论、变化等开始发生
senses.example: The remark sparked a heated debate.
senses.exampleCN: 这句话引发了一场激烈的争论。
senses.why: A spark starts a fire, so the verb came to mean starting anything.
senses.whyCN: 火星能点燃火焰，动词因此表示点燃任何事情。

senses.title: A trace of feeling
senses.definition: a small amount of a feeling such as hope or interest
senses.definitionCN: 希望、兴趣等情感的微小分量
senses.example: There was still a spark of hope in her eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 她眼中仍有一丝希望。
senses.why: A single spark can keep a fire alive, just as a trace keeps hope alive.
senses.whyCN: 一点火星能让火不灭，正如一丝念想让希望延续。

intro.en: Spark is an old English word for a flying bit of fire.
intro.cn: spark 是古英语中表示飞溅火粒的词。

items.en: Spearca meant a small burning particle.
items.cn: spearca 意为细小的燃烧颗粒。

items.en: The form became sparke, still a flying spark of fire.
items.cn: 词形变为 sparke，仍指飞溅的火星。

items.en: The verb meant to send out sparks.
items.cn: 动词形式表示迸出火星。

items.en: It grew figurative, meaning to set off an event.
items.cn: 它引申为引发某个事件。

items.en: A spark of hope borrowed the image of a surviving flame.
items.cn: a spark of hope 借用了火种不灭的意象。

note.en: Spark is compared with look-alike words and words for small flashes.
note.cn: 把 spark 与形近词以及表示细小闪光的词作比较。

normal.cn: 一点火星就足以点燃干草。

abstract.cn: 每一场大火都始于一点火星。

abstract.en: A spark is a promise made by fire.
abstract.cn: 火星是火焰许下的承诺。

abstract.en: Ideas spread like sparks in dry wind.
abstract.cn: 思想像干风中的火星一样蔓延。

core.en: A tiny point of fire that starts something.

branches.en: A bright grain jumps from the flames.
branches.cn: 一粒亮光从火焰中跳出。

branches.cn: 一句话让整个房间争论起来。

branches.en: A faint light remains in tired eyes.
branches.cn: 疲惫的眼中仍留着微弱的光。

branches.en: The fire grain and the quarrel share one beginning.
branches.cn: 火星与争吵共享同一个开端。

branches.cn: 点火与守候希望，都需要一点火星。

definition_en: a person with deep knowledge of one field, a doctor in one branch of medicine, or a shop dealing in one kind of goods
core_image: 一位医生摘下眼镜，指着心脏影像图向年轻同事讲解
scene: 她是心脏病方面的专家。She is a specialist in heart disease.
sceneCN: 这里 specialist 是「专家」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她是心脏病方面的专家。

senses.title: An expert
senses.definition: a person who knows a great deal about one subject
senses.definitionCN: 对某一学科了解极多的人
senses.example: She is a specialist in heart disease.
senses.exampleCN: 她是心脏病方面的专家。
senses.why: This is the general sense of a person narrowed to one field.
senses.whyCN: 这是把一个人限定在一个领域的通用含义。

senses.title: A medical expert
senses.definition: a doctor trained in one branch of medicine
senses.definitionCN: 受过某一医学分支训练的医生
senses.example: He was referred to a heart specialist.
senses.exampleCN: 他被转诊给一位心脏专科医生。
senses.why: Medicine adopted the word for doctors who limit their practice.
senses.whyCN: 医学界用这个词指限定执业范围的医生。

senses.title: A one-field shop
senses.definition: a shop or firm that deals in one kind of goods
senses.definitionCN: 只经营某一类商品的商店或公司
senses.example: The shop is a specialist in rare books.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店专营珍本书籍。
senses.why: A business can be a specialist by narrowing what it sells.
senses.whyCN: 商家通过缩小经营范围，也能成为某一领域的专门店。

intro.en: Specialist is special with the suffix for a person devoted to a field.
intro.cn: specialist 是 special 加上表示「专注于某领域的人」的后缀。

items.en: Specialis meant of a particular kind.
items.cn: specialis 意为属于某一特定种类的。

items.en: Spécialiste named one devoted to a single study.
items.cn: spécialiste 指专注于单一学问的人。

items.en: Specialist entered English in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: specialist 于十九世纪进入英语。

items.en: Medicine used it for doctors of one branch.
items.cn: 医学用它指某一分支的医生。

items.en: Shops and firms adopted it for narrow trade.
items.cn: 商店和公司用它表示专营某一类业务。

note.en: Specialist is compared with look-alike words and words for experts.
note.cn: 把 specialist 与形近词以及表示专家的词作比较。

normal.cn: 他被转诊给一位心脏专科医生。

normal.en: The shop is a specialist in rare books.

normal.en: Specialist training takes many years.
normal.cn: 专业培训需要很多年。

abstract.en: To specialize is to trade width for depth.
abstract.cn: 专精，是用广度换深度。

abstract.en: Every specialist was once a curious beginner.

abstract.en: The narrower the field, the deeper the well.
abstract.cn: 领域越窄，井就越深。

examples.en: The shop is a specialist in rare books.

core.en: A person or business narrowed to one field.

pos.zh: 专业化；专门化；专业领域；专化；（生物）特化（可数或不可数，指具体专业方向时用复数 specializations）

senses.title: Concentrating on one part
senses.titleCN: 专业化：把精力集中到某一环节
senses.definition: the process of concentrating effort on one narrow activity or field
senses.definitionCN: 把精力集中于某一狭窄活动或领域的过程
senses.example: Specialization raised output because each worker repeated one task.
senses.exampleCN: 专业化提高了产量，因为每个工人只重复一项任务。
senses.why: Latin specialis meant 'belonging to a particular kind', from species 'kind'; the -ization suffix names the process of becoming of one kind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 specialis 意为「属于某一类的」，出自 species「种类」；-ization 后缀命名「变得只属一类」的过程。

senses.title: A chosen field of expertise
senses.titleCN: 专业方向：个人或机构所专攻的领域
senses.definition: a particular field in which a person or institution has concentrated its work
senses.definitionCN: 个人或机构集中投入的某一特定领域
senses.example: Her specialization is the chemistry of soils.
senses.exampleCN: 她的专业方向是土壤化学。
senses.why: The process noun turned concrete: the result of concentrating is a field one can name and claim.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词具体化了：集中投入的结果变成一个可以命名并宣称的领域。

senses.title: Division of labour
senses.titleCN: 分工专业化：社会把任务拆给不同人
senses.definition: in economics, the arrangement in which different people or regions produce different goods
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中指不同人或地区生产不同商品的安排
senses.example: Trade grows when regional specialization is allowed to develop.
senses.exampleCN: 当地区专业化得以发展时，贸易就会增长。
senses.why: Economics generalized the workshop image: the unit that concentrates may be a region or a whole country.
senses.whyCN: 经济学推广了车间的意象：集中投入的单位可以是地区，甚至整个国家。

senses.title: Biological specialization
senses.titleCN: 生物特化：适应某一特定生态位
senses.definition: in biology, adaptation to a narrow ecological niche or function
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中指对狭窄生态位或功能的适应
senses.example: The beak shows extreme specialization for cracking one kind of seed.
senses.exampleCN: 这种喙极度特化，只适合咬开一种种子。
senses.why: Evolution reuses the 'one kind' sense: an organism narrowed to one resource is specialized, and the process is specialization.
senses.whyCN: 进化论沿用「只属一类」之义：被收窄到一种资源的生物就是特化的，这一过程即 specialization。

senses.title: Cellular differentiation
senses.titleCN: 细胞分化：一类细胞只承担一种功能
senses.definition: in developmental biology, the narrowing of a cell's role to one function
senses.definitionCN: 发育生物学中指细胞角色收窄为单一功能
senses.example: Specialization of cells makes a liver cell unable to become a nerve cell.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞的特化使肝细胞无法变成神经细胞。
senses.why: Here the word names loss as well as gain: gaining a function costs the ability to do others.
senses.whyCN: 此处这个词既指获得也指丧失：获得一种功能，代价是失去做其他事的能力。

senses.title: Medical specialty training
senses.titleCN: 医学专科化：由专科医生诊治
senses.definition: in medicine, the concentration of practice in one branch of care
senses.definitionCN: 医学中把诊疗集中于某一分支
senses.example: Specialization in surgery shortened recovery times.
senses.exampleCN: 外科的专科化缩短了康复时间。
senses.why: Professional training made the word an institutional label: a specialty is certified, and the process is specialization.
senses.whyCN: 专业训练把这个词变成建制标签：专科是被认证的，而这一过程就是 specialization。

senses.title: Specialization of function
senses.titleCN: 功能专门化：器官只做一件事
senses.definition: in anatomy and engineering, the assignment of one function to one part
senses.definitionCN: 解剖学与工程中指让一个部件只承担一种功能
senses.example: The heart's specialization for pumping left little tissue for anything else.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏对泵血功能的专门化，使它几乎没有余力做别的事。
senses.why: Function replaces field: the narrowing happens to an organ or a part, not to a person.
senses.whyCN: 功能取代了领域：收窄发生在器官或部件上，而非人身上。

senses.title: Narrowing of word meaning
senses.titleCN: 词义狭窄化：词只保留一个用法
senses.definition: in linguistics, the restriction of a word's meaning to a narrower sense
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中词义被限制到更窄的义项
senses.example: Specialization turned the general word for drink into the word for one beverage.
senses.exampleCN: 词义狭窄化把泛指饮料的词变成了专指某一种饮品的词。
senses.why: Linguistics borrowed the process word for semantic narrowing: a word too becomes specialized to one kind.
senses.whyCN: 语言学借这个表示过程的名词指语义收窄：一个词也会特化为只指一类。

senses.title: Narrow audience publishing
senses.titleCN: 窄众出版：面向特定读者
senses.definition: in media, the targeting of content at a small defined audience
senses.definitionCN: 媒体中把内容对准一小群明确受众
senses.example: Magazine specialization meant fewer readers but higher subscription prices.
senses.exampleCN: 杂志的窄众化意味着读者更少，但订阅价格更高。
senses.why: Media markets apply the same narrowing: a title aims at one kind of reader and survives on depth.
senses.whyCN: 媒体市场应用同样的收窄逻辑：一份刊物瞄准一类读者，靠深度生存。

intro.en: Specialization joins Latin specialis 'of a particular kind' with the English process suffix -ization. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: specialization 把拉丁 specialis「属于某一类的」与英语过程后缀 -ization 结合起来。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin species meant 'appearance, kind, sort'. It gave English species and special, and the deeper origin of the noun is debated.
items.cn: 拉丁 species 意为「外观、种类、类别」。它产生英语 species 与 special，其更深来源有争议。

items.en: Specialis 'belonging to a particular kind' was used in later Latin for what is peculiar to one thing rather than common to all.
items.cn: specialis「属于某一类的」在后世拉丁中用于表示某物独有的、而非共有的性质。

items.en: English formed verbs in -ize from adjectives, and the noun -ization followed. Specialize and specialization are English developments, not Latin words.
items.cn: 英语由形容词构成 -ize 动词，随后产生 -ization 名词。specialize 与 specialization 都是英语的发展，并非拉丁词。

items.en: The word spread with industrial division of labour and with the growth of professional disciplines, both of which rewarded narrow expertise.
items.cn: 这个词随工业分工与专业学科的成长而流行，这两者都奖励狭窄的专长。

items.en: Nineteenth-century biology applied the same word to organisms and cells, where narrowing to a niche is both an advantage and a constraint.
items.cn: 19 世纪生物学把同一个词用于生物体与细胞，在那里收窄到某一生态位既是优势也是限制。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation date only): the first English citation of specialization is uncertain and usually placed in the nineteenth century; the deeper origin of species is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：specialization 的英语首见书证存疑，通常定在 19 世纪；species 的更深来源属重构。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same species family that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms about narrowing.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 species 词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是表示收窄的近义词。

entries.definition: A person who concentrates on one field. Specialization is the process or the field itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指集中钻研某一领域的人。specialization 是过程或领域本身。

entries.definition: Means 'distinctive or for a particular purpose'. It shares the root but does not name a process of narrowing.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「特别的或专用的」。它共享词根，但不命名收窄的过程。

entries.definition: A detailed statement of requirements. It comes from species plus facere 'to make', so it shares the species root but adds the making verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指详细的要求说明。它由 species 加 facere「制造」构成，因此共享 species 词根，但多了「制造」动词。

entries.definition: A group of organisms able to interbreed. It is the source noun, while specialization names a process.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够互相繁殖的一群生物。它是源名词，而 specialization 命名一个过程。

entries.definition: The act of making something narrower. It is broader than specialization, which implies a field or function.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变窄的行为。它比 specialization 更宽泛，后者暗含领域或功能。

entries.definition: The focusing of attention or resources. It stresses effort gathered, while specialization stresses scope reduced.
entries.definitionCN: 注意力或资源的集中。它强调努力聚拢，而 specialization 强调范围缩小。

entries.definition: Deep skill in a field. It is what specialization produces, not the process of producing it.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一领域的深厚技能。它是 specialization 的产物，而非该过程本身。

entries.definition: The process of becoming different. In biology it overlaps with cell specialization, but it stresses distinction rather than narrowing.
entries.definitionCN: 变得不同的过程。在生物学中与细胞特化重叠，但它强调区别而非收窄。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: specialis 'of one kind' + -ization: the process of becoming one-kind.
normal.cn: specialis「属于一类的」+ -ization：变得只属一类的过程。

normal.en: The family runs special, specialize, specialized, specialization, specialist, specialty, species.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 special、specialize、specialized、specialization、specialist、specialty、species。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: specialization in, economic specialization, specialization of function.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：在……方面的专长、经济专业化、功能专门化。

normal.en: specialization is the process or the field; specialist is the person; special is the adjective.
normal.cn: specialization 是过程或领域；specialist 是人；special 是形容词。

normal.en: In biology the word cuts both ways: a specialist gains a niche and loses flexibility.
normal.cn: 在生物学中这个词有两面：专化者获得一个生态位，也失去灵活性。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one narrowing: effort, a word, a cell or a market becomes confined to one kind, and the word can name the process or the resulting field.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一次收窄展开：精力、词义、细胞或市场被限制到一类，而这个词既可命名过程，也可命名由此形成的领域。

branches.en: FIELD: the result is a named expertise, certified in professions like medicine.
branches.cn: 领域：结果是可命名的专长，在医学等职业中被认证。

branches.en: BIOLOGY: organisms, cells and organs narrow to one niche or function.

branches.en: LANGUAGE: a word's meaning narrows to one sense.
branches.cn: 语言：词义收窄到一个义项。

branches.en: MEDIA: content aims at one kind of reader.
branches.cn: 媒体：内容瞄准一类读者。

definition_en: to focus on one subject or kind of work, or to make something more focused

senses.title: To focus on a subject
senses.definition: to study or work on one subject in depth
senses.definitionCN: 深入学习或研究某一门学科
senses.example: She specializes in children's medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 她专攻儿童医学。
senses.why: This is the core modern sense of narrowing study.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代表示收窄研究范围的核心含义。

senses.title: To work in one line

definition_en: clearly described, exact, or relating to one particular thing
core_image: 一张清单上每一项都写得清清楚楚，旁边标着唯一的编号
scene: 请举一个具体的例子。Please give a specific example.
sceneCN: 这里 specific 是「具体的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请举一个具体的例子。

senses.title: Clearly stated
senses.definition: described in enough detail to be clear
senses.definitionCN: 描述得足够详细而清楚
senses.example: Please give a specific example.
senses.exampleCN: 请举一个具体的例子。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of detail rather than generality.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常表示细节而非笼统的含义。

senses.title: Exact
senses.definition: stated exactly, leaving no doubt
senses.definitionCN: 表述精确，不留疑问
senses.example: The instructions are very specific.

senses.why: Exactness is clarity pushed to a single answer.
senses.whyCN: 确切，是把清楚推到唯一答案。

senses.title: Of one thing only
senses.definition: relating to one particular thing and not others

senses.why: A detail that belongs to one thing marks it off from the rest.

intro.en: Specific came from Latin specificus, naming a thing by its kind.
intro.cn: specific 来自拉丁语 specificus，意为按种类来界定某物。

items.en: Species meant kind, and specificus meant of a kind.
items.cn: species 意为种类，specificus 意为属于某一种类的。

items.en: Specificus marked what belongs to one species alone.
items.cn: specificus 标记只属于某一物种的事物。

items.en: Specific entered English as the opposite of general.
items.cn: specific 作为 general 的反义词进入英语。

items.en: It came to mean exact in detail.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示细节上的确切。

items.en: It also named what is special to one thing.
items.cn: 它也指某一事物所特有的。

note.en: Specific is compared with look-alike words and words for exactness.
note.cn: 把 specific 与形近词以及表示确切的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Specific pins a thing down to clear detail or one case.
normalIntro.cn: specific 把事物钉在清楚的细节或某一个例子上。

normal.en: Please give a specific example.

normal.en: We met for a specific purpose.

normal.en: Each plant has specific needs for light.

abstract.en: The specific is where general truths become real.
abstract.cn: 普遍的道理，在具体之处才成为真实。

abstract.en: A specific name is a handle for an idea.
abstract.cn: 具体的名字是抓住念头的把手。

abstract.en: Vague words float; specific words land.
abstract.cn: 含糊的词漂浮，具体的词落地。

root: 来自晚期拉丁语 specificus（属于某一种类的），由 species（种类）加表示「制作、形成」的词根构成，核心义为按种类界定、具体明确。

sensesIntro.en: Specific means clearly detailed, exact, or belonging to one particular thing.
sensesIntro.cn: specific 指细节清楚的、确切的，或属于某一特定事物的。

core.en: Narrowed down to one clear case.
core.cn: 收窄到唯一清楚的情形。

branches.en: One example is named instead of a whole class.
branches.cn: 举出的是一个例子，而不是一整类。

branches.en: A rule leaves no room for doubt.

branches.en: One medicine seeks one virus only.

branches.en: Detail and exactness both narrow the meaning.

branches.en: Being exact is being limited to one thing.

intro.en: Specific forms adverbs, verbs, and nouns of exact statement.
intro.cn: specific 构成表示确切陈述的副词、动词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is specificus, of a kind, built on species.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 specificus（属于某一种类的），由 species 构成。

definition_zh: 规格；规格说明；详细要求；具体指明；专利说明书
definition_en: a detailed statement of what is required, or the act of stating requirements precisely
core_image: 一张图纸边缘写满尺寸、公差与材料标号，每一行都可被检验
scene: 这里指「规格」。 The supplier built the part to the specification, down to the stated tolerance.
sceneCN: 这里 specification 指「技术规格」（第 1 个义项：对尺寸、材料与公差的明确要求）；供应商严格按规格制造零件。图中可辨识物件：工程图、公差标注、材料清单、检验卡尺。

pos.zh: 规格；规格说明；详细要求；具体指明；专利说明书（可数，常用复数 specifications）

senses.title: A statement of requirements
senses.titleCN: 规格说明：把要求逐条写清
senses.definition: a detailed written statement of the requirements for a product or process
senses.definitionCN: 对产品或工艺要求的详细书面说明
senses.example: The specification lists every alloy and every tolerance.
senses.exampleCN: 规格说明列出了每种合金与每项公差。
senses.why: Late Latin specificatio came from specificare 'to specify', built on specificus 'making a kind', from species plus facere; the noun is a making-explicit.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁 specificatio 出自 specificare「具体指明」，后者基于 specificus「使成某类」，由 species 加 facere 构成；这个名词就是「把话说清楚」的产物。

senses.title: The act of specifying
senses.titleCN: 具体指明的动作：把模糊变明确
senses.definition: the act of stating something precisely rather than leaving it vague
senses.definitionCN: 把某事精确说明而非留作模糊的行为
senses.example: The specification of the boundary took three meetings.
senses.exampleCN: 边界的明确划定开了三次会。
senses.why: The action sense survives from Latin: specificatio named the act of making a thing specific.
senses.whyCN: 动作义承自拉丁：specificatio 命名的是「使某物变得具体」的行为。

senses.title: Engineering specification
senses.titleCN: 工程规格：可检验的技术参数
senses.definition: in engineering, the measured parameters a product must meet
senses.definitionCN: 工程中产品必须满足的可测量参数
senses.example: The beam failed because it was made below specification.
senses.exampleCN: 这根梁不合格，因为制造低于规格。
senses.why: Industry turned the document into measurable limits: a specification is what an inspector can check.
senses.whyCN: 工业把文件变成可测的限值：规格就是检验员可以核对的东西。

senses.title: A contract annex
senses.titleCN: 合同附件：作为验收依据
senses.definition: in construction and procurement, the document that defines acceptable work
senses.definitionCN: 建筑与采购中界定合格工作的文件
senses.example: The contractor must deliver to the specification in Annex B.
senses.exampleCN: 承包商必须按附件 B 的规格交付。
senses.why: Legally the document becomes binding: the specification is what a dispute is argued against.
senses.whyCN: 在法律上文件具有约束力：规格就是争议所依据的准绳。

senses.title: Patent specification
senses.titleCN: 专利说明书：充分公开技术要求
senses.definition: in patent law, the written description that must disclose the invention fully
senses.definitionCN: 专利法中必须充分公开发明的书面说明
senses.example: The patent specification must teach others how to build the device.
senses.exampleCN: 专利说明书必须教会儿他人如何制造该装置。
senses.why: Patent law uses the oldest sense: the applicant must specify the invention in enough detail to be reproduced.
senses.whyCN: 专利法使用最古老的义项：申请人必须把发明说明到足以被复现的程度。

senses.title: Software interface specification
senses.titleCN: 接口规范：约定数据如何交换
senses.definition: in computing, a document defining how systems exchange data
senses.definitionCN: 计算中界定系统如何交换数据的文件
senses.example: Two teams coded to the same specification and their modules linked.
senses.exampleCN: 两个团队按同一份规范编码，模块得以对接。
senses.why: Computing applies the contract sense to machines: an interface specification is a treaty between programs.
senses.whyCN: 计算把契约义用于机器：接口规范是程序之间的条约。

senses.title: Specification in linguistics
senses.titleCN: 语言学中的特征规定：对属性的明确标注
senses.definition: in linguistics, the explicit marking of a feature or property
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中对某一特征或属性的明确标注
senses.example: The specification of tense is obligatory in this language.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种语言中，时态的明确标注是强制的。
senses.why: Theoretical linguistics borrowed the word for explicit feature marking, the same 'making precise' move.
senses.whyCN: 理论语言学借这个词表示显性特征标注，仍是同一个「使之精确」的动作。

senses.title: Stating a condition
senses.definition: the explicit statement of a condition under which something holds
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物成立所依条件的明确陈述
senses.example: The specification of the test conditions matters more than the result.
senses.exampleCN: 试验条件的载明比结果本身更要紧。
senses.why: The word generalizes beyond products: any condition that must be stated precisely is specified.
senses.whyCN: 这个词超越产品而泛化：任何必须精确陈述的条件都被「载明」。

intro.en: Specification comes from Late Latin specificatio, from specificare 'to make specific', built on species 'kind' and facere 'to make'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: specification 出自晚期拉丁 specificatio，源自 specificare「使具体」，由 species「种类」与 facere「制造」构成。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Species meant 'appearance, kind'. The compound specificus described what makes a thing of its own kind; its deeper origin is debated.
items.cn: species 意为「外观、种类」。复合词 specificus 描述「使某物成为其自身那一类」的东西；其更深来源有争议。

items.en: Later Latin specificare meant 'to make specific, to name precisely'. The verb joined species with the facere family, so precision is pictured as making.
items.cn: 后世拉丁 specificare 意为「使具体、精确命名」。该动词把 species 与 facere 词族结合，因此「精确」被想象为一种制作。

items.en: The action noun specificatio named the act of specifying. It is a later Latin formation, not a classical word of wide use.
items.cn: 动作名词 specificatio 命名「具体说明」的行为。它属后世拉丁构词，并非古典中广泛使用的词。

items.en: English specification appears in the seventeenth century, first as the act of specifying and soon as a written statement. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 specification 于 17 世纪出现，先是「具体说明」的动作，随后很快指书面说明。最早确切书证年代存疑。

items.en: Nineteenth-century engineering and patent law made the document central: a specification became the measurable or legally binding statement of requirements.
items.cn: 19 世纪的工程与专利法让这份文件变得关键：specification 成为可测量或在法律上有约束力的要求陈述。

items.en: Source uncertain (first attestation date only): the first English date is uncertain; the origin of species before its 'kind' sense is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代存疑）：英语首见年代存疑；species 在「种类」义之前的来源属重构。

note.en: The first group holds species-family words that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for a statement of requirements.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 species 词族、易混淆的词；第二组是表示要求说明的近义词。

entries.definition: Means concentration on one field. Specification comes from species plus facere, so it names the making-explicit of requirements instead.
entries.definitionCN: 意为专注于某一领域。specification 由 species 加 facere 构成，命名的是把要求讲清楚。

entries.definition: Means 'precise or particular'. A specification is the document or act that makes something specific.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「具体的或特定的」。specification 是使某物变具体的那份文件或那个动作。

entries.definition: To state precisely. It names the act; specification is the act as a thing or the resulting document.
entries.definitionCN: 指精确说明。它命名动作；specification 是作为事物的动作或由此产生的文件。

entries.definition: A biological kind. It is the root noun but has no sense of requirement or precision.
entries.definitionCN: 指生物物种。它是词根名词，但不含要求或精确之义。

entries.definition: Something needed or demanded. A specification is the document that records requirements in detail.
entries.definitionCN: 指需要或要求的东西。specification 是把这些要求详细记录下来的文件。

entries.definition: An agreed rule or level. A standard is shared by a body; a specification may be written for one product.
entries.definitionCN: 共同商定的规则或水平。标准由团体共享；规格可以只针对一件产品。

entries.definition: A detailed plan or drawing. It shows the design, while a specification states the required properties.
entries.definitionCN: 详细的计划或图纸。它展示设计，而规格说明规定所需性能。

entries.definition: An account of what something is like. It need not be binding or measurable, as a specification usually is.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物样貌的叙述。它不必具有约束力或可测量性，而规格通常如此。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: species 'kind' + facere 'make' + -ation: making a thing specific.
normal.cn: species「种类」+ facere「制造」+ -ation：把事物做得具体明确。

normal.en: The family runs specify, specific, specifically, specified, specification, specificity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 specify、specific、specifically、specified、specification、specificity。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: technical specification, meet the specification, specification sheet.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：技术规格、符合规格、规格表。

normal.en: specialization and specification share species but split the work: one narrows effort, one states requirements.
normal.cn: specialization 与 specification 共享 species 但分工不同：一个收窄精力，一个写明要求。

normal.en: In patent law the specification must teach the invention, not merely claim it.
normal.cn: 在专利法中，说明书必须教会他人如何实现发明，而不仅是主张权利。

abstract.en: Picture a drawing whose margins are filled with numbers an inspector can check.
abstract.cn: 想象一张图纸，页边写满检验员可以核对的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a contract clause that turns 'good quality' into a measurable limit.
abstract.cn: 想象一条合同条款，把「质量好」变成可测的限值。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe that lists grams instead of 'some' and 'a little'.
abstract.cn: 想象一份食谱写的是克数，而不是「少许」「适量」。

examples.en: The bridge was built to a specification that allowed for high winds.
examples.cn: 这座桥按能承受强风的规格建造。

examples.en: Reviewers found that the specification omitted the operating temperature.
examples.cn: 评审者发现规格说明漏掉了工作温度。

examples.en: The patent specification described the pump in enough detail to rebuild it.
examples.cn: 专利说明书把泵描述得足以被重新制造出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「specific（具体的）+ ation（化）」——把要求变具体 → specification 规格说明

root: 拉丁 species「种类」+ facere「制造」→ specificare「使具体」→ specificatio「具体说明」→ 英语 specification。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of making precise: vague requirements are turned into written, measurable or legally binding statements, whether for a part, a contract, a patent or a program.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次「使之精确」的动作展开：模糊的要求被转成书面、可测或有法律约束力的陈述，无论对象是零件、合同、专利还是程序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drawing whose margins carry every dimension and tolerance.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张图纸，页边写满尺寸与公差。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT AND THE ACT: requirements are stated, and the stating is itself named.
branches.cn: 文件与动作：要求被陈述，而陈述本身也被命名。

branches.en: ENGINEERING AND LAW: the statement becomes measurable limits and a binding annex.
branches.cn: 工程与法律：陈述变成可测限值与有约束力的附件。

branches.en: PATENT: the oldest disclosure sense, where the description must teach the invention.
branches.cn: 专利：最古老的公开义，描述必须教会他人实现发明。

branches.en: COMPUTING: a specification is a treaty between programs.
branches.cn: 计算：规范是程序之间的条约。

branches.en: GENERAL PRECISION: features and test conditions must be marked explicitly.
branches.cn: 一般精确：特征与试验条件必须被显性标注。

intro.en: Specification is a Latin kind-word plus the making verb, closed by an action-noun suffix.
intro.cn: specification 是拉丁「种类」词加「制造」动词，再以动作名词后缀收尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin species 'kind' and facere 'to make' build specificare; -tio gives the action noun specificatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 species「种类」与 facere「制造」构成 specificare；-tio 产生动作名词 specificatio。

items.meaning: a making specific; a statement of requirements
items.exampleCN: 这份规格说明有四十页。

items.example: The rule applies specifically to ports.
items.exampleCN: 该规则特别适用于港口。
只能使用规定的润滑剂。

items.meaning: the quality of being precise or selective

items.exampleCN: 一个物种主导了这片礁区。

items.example: The part needs a special alloy.
items.exampleCN: 这个零件需要特殊合金。

definition_en: to state something clearly and exactly, or to name it as a requirement
core_image: 表格上的一栏被红笔圈出，旁边写着必须填写的具体内容
scene: 请在表格上注明你到达的日期。Please specify the date of your arrival on the form.
sceneCN: 这里 specify 是「明确说明、注明」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请在表格上注明你到达的日期。

senses.title: To state exactly
senses.definition: to say something clearly so there is no doubt
senses.definitionCN: 清楚说出，使人没有疑问
senses.example: Please specify the date of your arrival on the form.
senses.exampleCN: 请在表格上注明你到达的日期。
senses.why: This is the central modern sense of naming details exactly.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代表示确切说明细节的核心含义。

senses.title: To set as a rule
senses.definition: to state something as a required condition
senses.definitionCN: 把某事作为必要条件加以规定
senses.example: The contract specifies a two-week notice period.
senses.exampleCN: 合同规定了两周的通知期。
senses.why: A stated detail becomes a rule when it is written down.
senses.whyCN: 写下来的细节，就成了规定。

senses.title: To mark on a label
senses.definition: to state something on a product or document
senses.definitionCN: 在产品或文件上写明
senses.example: Each box must specify its weight.
senses.exampleCN: 每个箱子上都必须注明重量。
senses.why: A label that names its contents specifies them.
senses.whyCN: 写明内容的标签，就是在注明。

intro.en: Specify came from medieval Latin specificare, to name by kind.
intro.cn: specify 来自中世纪拉丁语 specificare，意为按种类指明。

items.en: Species meant kind or appearance.

items.en: Specificare meant to name a thing by its kind.

items.en: Labels used it for weights and contents.

normal.en: The rules clearly specify what is allowed.
normal.cn: 规则明确说明了允许的范围。

normal.en: Unless otherwise specified, all prices include tax.
normal.cn: 除非另有说明，所有价格都含税。

abstract.en: A vague wish cannot be carried out.
abstract.cn: 含糊的愿望无法被执行。

abstract.en: To name the detail is to take half the action.
abstract.cn: 点明细节，就等于完成了行动的一半。

abstract.en: What is left unspecified will be argued over.
abstract.cn: 没有说明的部分，终将引起争论。

root: 来自中世纪拉丁语 specificare（按种类指明），源于 species（种类、外观），核心义为把事物具体指名，使其不再含糊。

definition_en: a small part or example of something kept or tested to show what the whole is like
core_image: 玻璃罐里泡着一片叶子，标签上写着采集地点与日期
scene: 科学家把一片叶子做成标本。The scientist made a specimen from a leaf.

senses.title: A kept example
senses.definition: a part of a plant or animal kept for study
senses.definitionCN: 保存下来供研究的动植物部分
senses.example: The scientist made a specimen from a leaf.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家把一片叶子做成标本。
senses.why: This is the museum and laboratory sense of the word.

senses.title: A sample for testing

senses.example: The lab tested a blood specimen.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室检测了一份血液样本。
senses.why: Anything taken for testing acts as a specimen.
senses.whyCN: 任何取出供检测的东西都充当样本。

senses.title: A type of person
senses.definition: a person considered as an example of a kind, often humorously
senses.definitionCN: 作为某类范例的人，常带幽默意味
senses.example: The coach called him a fine specimen.
senses.exampleCN: 教练称他是个体格健壮的好苗子。
senses.why: Informal speech treats a strong person like a fine sample.
senses.whyCN: 口语把强壮的人比作上好的样本。

definition_zh: 光谱；波谱；范围，幅度；（意见、症状等的）整个序列，谱系
definition_en: the band of colours or wavelengths produced when light is dispersed, or a full range of related things
core_image: 一束白光穿过棱镜，在墙上摊成由红到紫的连续彩带，两端渐渐变暗
scene: 一束白光穿过棱镜，在墙上摊成由红到紫的连续彩带，两端渐渐变暗。A prism spread the spectrum across the wall in ordered bands.
sceneCN: 这里 spectrum 指「白光经色散后形成的彩色光带」（第 1 个义项：由不同波长按序排列成的可见色带）；句意为棱镜把光谱摊在墙上，形成有次序的条带。可辨识物件：棱镜、白光束、墙面彩带、暗边。

pos.zh: 光谱；波谱；范围；序列，谱系

senses.title: The colour band from a prism
senses.titleCN: 棱镜色散出的彩色光带
senses.definition: the band of colours seen when white light is dispersed, arranged from red through violet
senses.definitionCN: 白光被色散后出现的彩色带，从红到紫依次排列
senses.example: A prism spread the spectrum across the wall in ordered bands.
senses.exampleCN: 棱镜把光谱摊在墙上，形成有次序的条带。
senses.why: Latin spectrum meant an appearance or image, and Newton applied it to the coloured image thrown by a prism.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 spectrum 意为「外观、影像」，牛顿把这个词用于棱镜投出的彩色影像。

senses.title: The full range of wavelengths
senses.titleCN: 全部波长的范围，含不可见波段
senses.definition: the complete range of radiation, from radio waves through visible light to gamma rays
senses.definitionCN: 从无线电波经可见光到伽马射线的完整辐射范围
senses.example: The electromagnetic spectrum extends far beyond what the eye can see.
senses.exampleCN: 电磁波谱远远超出肉眼可见的范围。
senses.why: once invisible bands were discovered, the colour band widened into a continuum of wavelengths.
senses.whyCN: 不可见波段被发现后，原本的彩色带扩展成了连续的波长范围。

senses.title: A range of values
senses.titleCN: 数值或程度的范围、幅度
senses.definition: a continuous range between two extremes, as of sizes, doses or prices
senses.definitionCN: 在两个极端之间连续分布的范围，如尺寸、剂量或价格
senses.example: The clinic treats a wide spectrum of injuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所处理范围很广的各种损伤。
senses.why: the image of ordered bands becomes a scale on which a whole set of cases can be placed.
senses.whyCN: 有次序的条带这一形象，变成了一把可以安放一整组情况的标尺。

senses.title: A range of opinions
senses.titleCN: 意见的整个分布或谱系
senses.definition: the full spread of views held by a group, from one extreme to the other
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体所持看法的完整分布，从一端到另一端
senses.example: The committee heard a spectrum of opinion before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在表决前听取了各种不同意见。
senses.why: politics borrowed the word because opinions, like colours, arrange themselves in a gradation rather than in two blocks.
senses.whyCN: 政治借用这个词，因为意见像颜色一样呈渐变排列，而不是只分两块。

senses.title: A continuum of traits
senses.definition: a continuous range of a condition or trait, as in autism spectrum or a spectrum of severity
senses.definitionCN: 某种状况或特征的连续分布，如自闭症谱系或严重程度谱系
senses.example: The diagnosis sits on a spectrum rather than at a fixed point.
senses.exampleCN: 这一诊断位于一个连续谱系上，而不在某个固定点上。
senses.why: medicine took the word to replace sharp categories with a graded range, keeping the sense of ordered bands.
senses.whyCN: 医学用这个词取代非此即彼的分类，保留「有次序条带」的含义，表示渐变范围。

senses.title: A line spectrum
senses.titleCN: 线状谱：由一条条分立的亮线或暗线构成
senses.definition: a spectrum made of discrete bright or dark lines at specific wavelengths rather than a continuous band
senses.definitionCN: 由特定波长上一条条分立亮线或暗线构成的谱
senses.example: The line spectrum of hydrogen became the key to atomic theory.
senses.exampleCN: 氢的线状谱成了原子理论的关键。
senses.why: when a hot gas emits only certain wavelengths, the continuous band breaks into lines and the word still names the result.
senses.whyCN: 热气体只放出特定波长时，连续带断成一条条线，而这个词仍旧称呼这一结果。

senses.title: The frequency content of a signal
senses.titleCN: 信号的频谱：各频率成分的分布
senses.definition: the distribution of a signal across frequencies, shown as peaks on a frequency axis
senses.definitionCN: 信号在各频率上的分布，以频率轴上的峰显示
senses.example: The engineer looked for the hum in the spectrum of the recording.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在录音的频谱里寻找那阵嗡鸣。
senses.why: Fourier analysis turned a signal into ordered components, exactly the arrangement the older word already described.
senses.whyCN: 傅里叶分析把信号拆成有次序的成分，正是旧词原本描述的那种排列。

senses.title: Abstract: the whole extent of something
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：某事物的全部幅度与全部层次
senses.definition: the entire extent of a thing, from its lowest to its highest level, considered as one ordered whole
senses.definitionCN: 某物从最低到最高层次的全部幅度，被当作一个有次序的整体
senses.example: The exhibition covers the spectrum of the artist career, from student sketches to late murals.
senses.exampleCN: 展览涵盖这位艺术家创作生涯的全部层次，从学生素描到晚期刊画。
senses.why: the abstract sense drops the light and keeps only the span, so any complete gradation can be called a spectrum.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义去掉光，只留跨度，因此任何完整的渐变都可以称为 spectrum。

intro.en: Spectrum is Latin for appearance or image, from specere to look. Newton made it an optical term in 1671, and it later widened into every ordered range.
intro.cn: spectrum 在拉丁语中指「外观、影像」，出自 specere「看」。牛顿 1671 年使它成为光学词，后来它扩展到一切有次序的范围。

items.en: Specere meant to look at or observe; it also stands behind specimen, spectacle, speculate and perspective.
items.cn: specere 意为「看、观察」；specimen、spectacle、speculate 与 perspective 也出自它。

items.en: The noun spectrum named an appearance or image, especially a ghostly one; English spectre descends from the same form.
items.cn: 名词 spectrum 指「外观、影像」，尤指幽灵般的影像；英语 spectre 同出这一形式。

items.en: In his New Theory about Light and Colours Newton used spectrum for the coloured band thrown by a prism, and the optical sense fixed the word in science.
items.cn: 牛顿在《关于光与色的新理论》中用 spectrum 指棱镜投出的彩色带，这一光学义使该词在科学中固定下来。

items.en: Spectral lines and the discovery of invisible radiation extended spectrum from a colour band to the whole range of wavelengths.
items.cn: 谱线的研究与不可见辐射的发现，把 spectrum 从彩色带扩展到全部波长范围。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word spread to opinions, disease traits, political positions and any graded set.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词扩展到意见、疾病特征、政治立场以及任何渐变集合。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin shape of specere has no agreed derivation, so its link to the Indo-European root commonly cited for seeing is a reconstruction rather than a proven step.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：specere 在拉丁语之前的形式没有公认的派生路径，因此它与常被引用的「看」这一印欧词根的联系属重构，而非已证实的环节。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin root specere but now far apart in meaning; group two holds the range words that overlap the modern uses of spectrum.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 specere、如今意义却相去甚远的词；第二组是与 spectrum 现代用法重叠的范围类词。

entries.definition: The same Latin word in its older sense of a ghostly apparition; the British spelling keeps the Latin -re.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个拉丁词，保留其「幽灵影像」的旧义；英式拼写保留拉丁的 -re 形式。

entries.definition: From specere through a noun meaning something shown; it is a sample, not a range.
entries.definitionCN: 经一个表示「展示之物」的名词出自 specere；它指样品，不指范围。

entries.definition: From specula, a watchtower: to look out and reason about what cannot be seen directly.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 specula「瞭望塔」：向外眺望，并对无法直接看见之事作推断。

entries.definition: From spectare, to watch: something striking enough to draw a crowd of eyes.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 spectare「观看」：夺目到足以引来一片目光的事物。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the distance between limits; spectrum adds the idea of ordered gradation.
entries.definitionCN: 表示上下限之间跨度的日常词；spectrum 多了「有次序的渐变」这一层。

entries.definition: The full series of notes or colours; it stresses completeness where spectrum stresses spread.
entries.definitionCN: 音符或颜色的完整系列；强调完整，而 spectrum 强调铺开的跨度。

entries.definition: A continuous sequence with no breaks; a spectrum may be continuous or broken into lines.
entries.definitionCN: 没有间断的连续序列；而 spectrum 既可以是连续的，也可以断成谱线。

entries.definition: An impressive or ordered display of things; it lacks the physical band image of spectrum.
entries.definitionCN: 事物的有序陈列；它没有 spectrum 那种物理光带的形象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin root, the real Newtonian sense and the real modern extensions.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的牛顿义，以及真实的现代扩展。

normal.en: Spectrum and spectre share one Latin source: both name an appearance.
normal.cn: spectrum 与 spectre 共享一个拉丁来源：两者都指「显现之物」。

normal.en: Newton gave the word its colour-band sense in 1671.
normal.cn: 牛顿在 1671 年赋予它彩色带的意义。

normal.en: The plural is spectra, following the Latin neuter pattern.
normal.cn: 复数按拉丁中性词模式作 spectra。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range uses: broad spectrum, spectrum of opinion.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围义：广谱、意见的分布范围。

normal.en: The adjective spectral can mean both of a spectrum and ghostly.
normal.cn: 形容词 spectral 既可指「光谱的」，也可指「幽灵般的」。

abstract.en: Picture a street of houses shading from one colour at each end to another in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街的房子，从两端的一种颜色渐渐过渡到中间的另一种颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a choir arranged by pitch so that every voice finds a place.
abstract.cn: 想象一个按音高排列的合唱团，每条嗓子都能找到位置。

abstract.en: Picture a single note struck, then split into all the notes it contains.
abstract.cn: 想象敲响一个音，再把它拆成其中包含的所有音。

examples.en: The visible spectrum runs from about four hundred to seven hundred nanometres.
examples.cn: 可见光谱大约从四百纳米延伸到七百纳米。

examples.en: Their tastes cover a spectrum from plain folk songs to electronic noise.
examples.cn: 他们的口味覆盖从朴素民歌到电子噪音的整个范围。

examples.en: A spectrum analyser showed a strong peak at fifty hertz.
examples.cn: 频谱分析仪显示出五十赫兹处有一个强峰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「spectr（看）+ um」——眼睛看到的一条条颜色 → 光谱；引申为一条条排开的整个范围

root: 拉丁 spectrum「外观、影像」，出自 specere「看、观察」；specere 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定。英语 spectrum，复数 spectra。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the colour band, widen to all wavelengths, then slide into ranges of values, opinions and traits, then to line and signal spectra, and end with any complete gradation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项以彩色带开始，扩展到全部波长，再滑入数值、意见与特征的范围，接着到线状谱与信号频谱，最后落在任何完整的渐变上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white beam broken into bands that stay in order from one end to the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束白光断成若干条带，从一端到另一端始终保持次序。

branches.en: THE OPTICAL CORE: Newton's prism image is still the literal centre of the word.
branches.cn: 光学核心：牛顿的棱镜影像仍是这个词最字面的中心。

branches.en: BAND AND LINES: invisible bands and discrete lines are two shapes the same spectrum can take.
branches.cn: 带与线：不可见波段与分立谱线，是同一个光谱可以呈现的两种形状。

branches.en: GRADED SCALE: values and traits are placed along a span instead of in two boxes.
branches.cn: 渐变标尺：数值与特征被放在一段跨度上，而不是装进两个格子。

branches.en: POLITICAL SPREAD: opinions arrange themselves like colours, from one edge to the other.
branches.cn: 意见分布：意见像颜色一样，从一端排到另一端。

branches.en: SIGNAL AND WHOLE: a signal decomposed by frequency, and any complete extent, keep only the sense of ordered parts.
branches.cn: 信号与整体：按频率拆开的信号、以及任何完整幅度，都只保留「有次序的各个部分」这一层。

intro.en: Spectrum is a single Latin noun, but the root specere also builds a large English family whose members drifted far apart.
intro.cn: spectrum 是一个拉丁名词，但其词根 specere 还构成一个庞大的英语词族，成员意义已漂得很远。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun is spectrum, spectri, with specere as its verb. Spectre, specimen and speculate are relatives, not compounds of spectrum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词是 spectrum、spectri，其动词为 specere。spectre、specimen 与 speculate 是它的亲属词，而不是 spectrum 的复合词。

items.example: The spectrum lay across the wall in bands.
items.exampleCN: 光谱以条带形式横在墙上。

items.example: The two spectra overlapped near the red end.
items.exampleCN: 两条光谱在红端附近重叠。
这两个光源在光谱上不同。

items.example: The spectroscope showed the band directly.
items.exampleCN: 分光镜直接显示出光带。

definition_en: to guess about something without firm evidence, to think deeply, or to risk money on a possible profit
core_image: 几个人围在桌旁低声讨论一个尚无答案的问题，桌上摊着零散的线索
scene: 人们猜测他突然辞职的原因。People speculated about why he suddenly resigned.
sceneCN: 这里 speculate 是「推测、猜测」（第 1 个义项）；句意：人们猜测他突然辞职的原因。

senses.title: To guess
senses.definition: to form an opinion without firm evidence
senses.definitionCN: 在没有确凿证据的情况下形成看法
senses.example: People speculated about why he suddenly resigned.
senses.exampleCN: 人们猜测他突然辞职的原因。
senses.why: This is the central modern sense of guessing.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代表示猜测的核心含义。

senses.title: To think deeply
senses.definition: to think about a subject in a deep or abstract way
senses.definitionCN: 以深入或抽象的方式思考某一主题
senses.example: The philosopher speculated about the nature of time.
senses.exampleCN: 这位哲学家沉思时间的本质。
senses.why: The older sense names quiet thought rather than guesswork.
senses.whyCN: 更古老的含义指安静的思考，而非猜测。

senses.title: To risk money
senses.definition: to buy something hoping to sell it at a profit
senses.definitionCN: 买进某物，期望以更高价卖出获利
senses.example: He speculated in property and lost money.
senses.exampleCN: 他炒房产赔了钱。
senses.why: A guess about prices turned into a financial gamble.
senses.whyCN: 对价格的猜测，变成了金融上的赌博。

intro.en: Speculate came from Latin speculari, to watch from a high place.
intro.cn: speculate 来自拉丁语 speculari，意为从高处观察。

items.en: Specula meant a watchtower.
items.cn: specula 意为瞭望塔。

items.en: Speculari meant to watch or observe closely.
items.cn: speculari 意为观看或仔细观察。

items.en: Speculate entered English meaning to observe mentally.
items.cn: speculate 以在头脑中观察之义进入英语。

items.en: It came to mean forming opinions without proof.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示在没有证据时形成看法。

items.en: Finance used it for risky buying and selling.
items.cn: 金融领域用它表示有风险的买卖。

note.en: Speculate is compared with look-alike words and verbs of guessing.
note.cn: 把 speculate 与形近词以及表示猜测的动词作比较。

entries.definition: to give an answer without certainty
to risk money on a result

normalIntro.en: To speculate is to lean over the edge of what is known.
normalIntro.cn: speculate 就是伏在已知边缘向下张望。

normal.en: People speculated about why he suddenly resigned.
normal.cn: 人们猜测他突然辞职的原因。

normal.en: The philosopher speculated about the nature of time.
normal.cn: 这位哲学家沉思时间的本质。

normal.en: He speculated in property and lost money.
normal.cn: 他炒房产赔了钱。

normal.en: Reporters speculated on the result of the talks.
normal.cn: 记者们推测会谈的结果。

normal.en: It is useless to speculate without evidence.
normal.cn: 没有证据的猜测毫无用处。

abstract.en: Speculation is a bridge built before the river is found.
abstract.cn: 推测是在找到河之前就架起的桥。

abstract.en: The market rewards those who guess and punishes those who are sure.
abstract.cn: 市场奖励猜测者，惩罚确信者。

abstract.en: A mind that speculates is a mind that is still moving.
abstract.cn: 仍在推测的心，是仍在运动的心。

examples.en: People speculated about why he suddenly resigned.
examples.cn: 人们猜测他突然辞职的原因。

examples.en: The philosopher speculated about the nature of time.
examples.cn: 这位哲学家沉思时间的本质。

examples.en: He speculated in property and lost money.
examples.cn: 他炒房产赔了钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: speculate 源自拉丁语 speculari（从瞭望塔观察），表示「推测、猜测」，也指「沉思」和「投机」；speculation 是「推测、投机」，speculative 是「推测的、投机性的」，speculator 是「投机者」。

root: 来自拉丁语 speculari（观察、窥探），源于 specula（瞭望塔），本义为从高处远望，后引申为在头脑中推想，再到金融上的投机。

sensesIntro.en: Speculate means to guess without proof, to think deeply, or to risk money on a profit.
sensesIntro.cn: speculate 指无证据地猜测、深入思考，或为获利而冒险买卖。

core.en: Looking past the edge of the known.
core.cn: 越过已知的边界向外看。

branches.en: People trade rumours in a low voice.
branches.cn: 人们低声交换传闻。

branches.en: A thinker sits alone with a question.
branches.cn: 思想家独自与一个问题对坐。

branches.en: A buyer bets on rising house prices.
branches.cn: 买家押注房价上涨。

branches.en: Guessing and gambling both begin with uncertainty.
branches.cn: 猜测与投机都始于不确定。

branches.en: Idle guessing and deep thought differ only in patience.
branches.cn: 闲猜与深思，只差在耐心。

intro.en: Speculate builds a family of guessing and risking words.
intro.cn: speculate 构成表示猜测与冒险的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is speculari, to observe, from specula, a watchtower.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 speculari（观察），源于 specula（瞭望塔）。

items.example: People speculated about why he suddenly resigned.
items.exampleCN: 人们猜测他突然辞职的原因。

items.example: The paper speculates about a merger.
items.exampleCN: 报纸推测将有一次合并。

items.example: Stop speculating and check the facts.

items.meaning: a guess or a risky deal
a person who gambles on prices
items.exampleCN: 投机者低价买下了土地。

items.example: He spoke speculatively about the cause.
items.exampleCN: 他推测性地谈到了原因。

definition_zh: 推测；猜测；投机（尤指在金融市场上押注价格变化）
definition_en: the forming of a judgment without firm evidence, or the buying and selling of assets in the hope of gain from price changes
core_image: 一个人站在高塔上举着望远镜看远方，塔下同时摆着一张押注单和一本笔记
scene: 央行声明发布前，老交易员盯着行情屏加仓，赌利率会往下走。The old trader added to his position before the statement, pure speculation on falling rates.
sceneCN: 这里指「在信息不足时押注价格走向的金融投机」（第 2 个义项：买进或卖出资产，赌未来价格变化带来收益）；句意为声明发布之前，这位老交易员加仓，纯粹是在赌利率下行。可辨识物件：行情屏、望远镜、押注单、笔记本。

pos.zh: 推测；猜测；投机（可数或不可数，复数 speculations）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁分词词干加动词后缀 → 推测；投机
由该动词加形容词后缀，义为「倾向于……」→ 推测的；投机性的
由该动词加施事后缀 → 投机者；推测者
由形容词加副词后缀 → 凭推测地；投机地
由形容词加名词后缀，表性质 → 推测性；投机性

senses.title: A theory built without firm evidence
senses.titleCN: 在证据不足时形成的推断
senses.definition: a judgment or opinion formed about something that is not yet known for certain
senses.definitionCN: 对尚未确定之事形成的判断或看法
senses.example: Her speculation that the meeting would be postponed proved correct.
senses.exampleCN: 她关于会议将推迟的推测后来被证明是对的。
senses.why: the word names the act of looking out from a height, so the core is seeing what is not yet in front of you, then guessing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本指从高处向外瞭望，核心是先看见尚未到眼前的事，再去猜。

senses.title: Betting on price movements in markets
senses.titleCN: 在金融市场上押注价格变化
senses.definition: the practice of buying or selling an asset in the hope of a profit from a price change rather than from its use
senses.definitionCN: 买进或卖出资产，指望从价格变化而非使用中获得利润的做法
senses.example: Heavy speculation in copper drove the price far above its production cost.
senses.exampleCN: 对铜的大量投机把价格推到远高于生产成本的水平。
senses.why: finance kept the looking-ahead image but made the guess a position: money is placed on a future price.
senses.whyCN: 金融保留了「向前看」的意象，却把猜测变成头寸：把钱押在一个未来价格上。

senses.title: A single offered guess
senses.titleCN: 一次具体的猜测或说法
senses.definition: one countable guess or opinion that a person puts forward
senses.definitionCN: 某个人提出的一个可数猜测或看法
senses.example: The report's central speculation is that the tomb was robbed in antiquity.
senses.exampleCN: 该报告的核心猜测是这座墓在古代就被盗过。
senses.why: because one guess is a countable thing, the noun takes a plural and can be introduced by a or the.
senses.whyCN: 因为一个猜测是可数之物，这个名词有复数形式，也能用不定冠词或定冠词引出。

senses.title: Talk about other people's private affairs
senses.titleCN: 对他人私事的议论与猜测
senses.definition: idle or intrusive guessing about someone's private life, often treated as a mild vice
senses.definitionCN: 对他人私生活作出的闲散或侵入式猜测，常被视为轻度的不良习惯
senses.example: The tabloids fed speculation about the couple's separation.
senses.exampleCN: 小报助长了关于这对夫妇分居的猜测。
senses.why: the same word covers guessing that has no financial stake at all, which is why it also names gossip.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也涵盖完全无关金钱的猜测，因此也指闲话。

senses.title: Pure reasoning about what cannot be observed
senses.titleCN: 对无法观察之物进行的纯粹思辨
senses.definition: reasoning that follows a question beyond the reach of observation, as in philosophy and theology
senses.definitionCN: 把问题推到观察所不能及之处进行推理，如哲学与神学中的思辨
senses.example: Medieval speculation on the nature of light drew on both optics and scripture.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪关于光的本质的思辨同时借助光学与经文。
senses.why: the sense is old and respectable: when the object cannot be seen, looking out from the tower becomes careful thought.
senses.whyCN: 这一义既古老又体面：当对象看不见时，从塔上向外看就变成了审慎的思考。

senses.title: Buying property to profit from its price
senses.titleCN: 为从房价上涨中获利而买房
senses.definition: the purchase of land or buildings mainly to resell at a higher price
senses.definitionCN: 主要为以更高价转手而购买土地或房屋
senses.example: Speculation in land on the city's edge pushed prices beyond local wages.
senses.exampleCN: 对城市边缘土地的投机把价格推高到超过当地工资的水平。
senses.why: property is the classic case where use value is small and expected gain is large, so the financial sense attaches easily.
senses.whyCN: 房产是使用价值小、预期收益大的典型情形，金融义便自然附着上来。

senses.title: Holding an asset for gain, not for use
senses.titleCN: 持有资产为了获利而非使用
senses.definition: in economics, the demand for an asset or for cash because a price is expected to rise
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中因预期价格上升而产生对资产或现金的需求
senses.example: Keynes described the speculative motive for holding cash when bond yields are expected to rise.
senses.exampleCN: 凯恩斯描述过在预期债券收益率上升时持有现金的投机动机。
senses.why: economics separated the holding motive from the trading act, so the word now also labels a reason for keeping an asset idle.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把持有动机与交易动作分开，这个词于是也标注「让资产闲置」的一种理由。

senses.title: The old sense of watching from a height
senses.titleCN: 古代「从高处观察」的本义
senses.definition: the historical sense of observing or spying from a lookout point, now archaic
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指从瞭望点观察或窥探，今已古旧
senses.example: The Latin noun first meant a lookout, and only later a guess.
senses.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词最初指瞭望处，后来才指猜测。
senses.why: keeping this older layer explains the spelling: the tower is still visible inside the modern word.
senses.whyCN: 保留这一更早的层次能解释拼写：现代词里仍看得见那座塔。

intro.en: Speculation comes from Latin speculatio 'a lookout, a watching', from speculari 'to watch, to spy', built on specula 'watchtower', itself from specere 'to look'. The financial sense is a later narrowing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: speculation 来自拉丁 speculatio「瞭望、观察」，出自动词 speculari「观察、窥探」，其词干 specula 意为「瞭望塔」，再上溯 specere「看」。金融义是后来收窄的结果。年代均为约数。

items.en: Specere meant 'to look, to observe'. Its older Indo-European history is reconstructed rather than directly attested, and the same stock also gives words for inspecting and for spectacle.
items.cn: specere 意为「看、观察」。它更早的印欧语历史属于重构而非直接有证，同一词干还给出「检查」与「景象」等词。

items.en: A specula was a watchtower or lookout, the raised place from which a guard could see approaching danger.
items.cn: specula 指瞭望塔或观察哨，即守卫能看见危险逼近的高处。

items.en: The verb speculari meant 'to watch from a height, to spy, to examine', and it kept the sense of purposeful looking rather than mere seeing.
items.cn: 动词 speculari 意为「从高处观察、窥探、审视」，保留的是有目的的看，而非单纯的看见。

items.en: The noun speculatio named both the act of watching and, by extension, the conclusions a watcher might form about what was coming.
items.cn: 名词 speculatio 既指观察的动作，也引申指观察者对将发生之事可能形成的结论。

items.en: English took the noun in the fourteenth century as speculation. Early uses covered observation, inquiry and conjecture on matters hard to see.
items.cn: 英语于 14 世纪以 speculation 吸收该名词。早期用法涵盖观察、探究与对难以看见之事的猜想。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word was applied to ventures whose return depended on a future price, and by the nineteenth century this was the dominant commercial sense.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，这个词被用于收益取决于未来价格的事业；到 19 世纪，这已成为主要的商业义。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same looking root or close in shape; the second holds words for guessing and for betting, each with a different weight.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「看」这个词根或形近的词；第二组是猜测与押注类近义词，分量各不相同。

entries.definition: To form a guess or to take a market position; the noun names either the guess or the position.
entries.definitionCN: 指作出猜测或建立市场头寸；名词则指猜测或头寸本身。

entries.definition: Based on guesswork or carrying financial risk; it describes the quality, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指基于猜测或带有金融风险；它描述性质，而非动作。

entries.definition: One who takes such positions; the noun speculation names what that person does.
entries.definitionCN: 指建立此类头寸的人；名词投机则指此人所做的事。

entries.definition: Specere 'to look' plus a suffix gave a public show; the sense is passive seeing, not guessing.
entries.definitionCN: 「看」的词根加后缀给出「公开景象」；其义为被动地看见，而非猜测。

entries.definition: To look closely into something for a purpose; it lacks the forward, uncertain reach of speculation.
entries.definitionCN: 指为某目的仔细查看；它缺少投机那种朝前、不确定的延伸。

entries.definition: A conclusion offered on incomplete grounds; it stresses the weakness of the evidence more than speculation does.
entries.definitionCN: 指在证据不完整时提出的结论；它比投机更强调证据薄弱。

entries.definition: A stated proposition put up for testing; it is meant to be checked, while speculation may never be.
entries.definitionCN: 指为检验而提出的明确命题；它本就打算被验证，而猜测未必。

entries.definition: Staking money on a random outcome; speculation at least claims a reading of the market.
entries.definitionCN: 指把钱押在随机结果上；投机至少声称读过市场。

entries.definition: Money put into an asset for income or long-term growth; the line between it and speculation is drawn by intent and risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指为收益或长期增长投入资产的钱；它与投机的界线由意图与风险划定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The tower is still inside the word: a watcher on a high platform guesses what is coming.
normal.cn: 那座塔仍在词里：高台上的观察者猜测将要发生什么。

normal.en: The family runs speculate, speculation, speculative, speculator, speculatively.
normal.cn: 同族词包括推测、猜测、推测性的、投机者、凭推测地。

normal.en: Fixed phrases separate the kinds: pure speculation, market speculation, speculation in property.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把类型分开：纯属猜测、市场投机、房地产投机。

normal.en: The same looking root appears in inspect and spectacle, both about seeing rather than betting.
normal.cn: 同一个「看」的词根出现在检查与景象二词中，二者都关乎看见而非押注。

normal.en: Finance marks the difference by intent: use the asset and it is investment; wait for its price and it is speculation.
normal.cn: 金融业以意图划界：使用资产叫投资，等它的价格叫投机。

abstract.en: Picture a guard in a tower before dawn, guessing which road the carts will take.
abstract.cn: 想象天没亮时塔上的守卫，猜运货的车会走哪条路。

abstract.en: Picture a coin held above a table, neither side yet showing.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币悬在桌面上方，哪一面都还没露出。

abstract.en: Picture a row of house shells with no families in them, bought only for the price tag.
abstract.cn: 想象一排没有住户的空壳房，买下它们只为那张价签。

examples.en: Speculation about the cause of the fire filled the newspapers for a week.
examples.cn: 关于起火原因的猜测在报纸上持续了一周。

examples.en: The tax was meant to curb speculation in empty apartments.
examples.cn: 这项税意在遏制对空置公寓的投机。

examples.en: Without data, any explanation of the collapse remains speculation.
examples.cn: 没有数据，对这次崩塌的任何解释都只是猜测。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「看」的词根加名词后缀——站在塔上往远处看，看不清就只好猜；把钱押在猜的结果上就是投机

root: 拉丁 speculatio「瞭望、观察」来自 speculari（specula「瞭望塔」+ specere「看」）；同根词有 inspect、spectacle、perspective；金融义为 18 至 19 世纪的收窄。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from one posture: a watcher on a height looks at what has not arrived. The looking becomes a guess, the guess becomes talk, then thought, then a position in a market, then a reason to hold an asset.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一个姿态出发：观察者站在高处，看向尚未到来的事。看变成猜测，猜测变成议论，再变成思辨，再变成市场上的头寸，最后变成持有资产的理由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a watcher on a tower looks toward a future he cannot yet see clearly.
core.cn: 核心意象：塔上的观察者朝一个还看不清楚的未来望去。

branches.en: THE ORIGINAL POSTURE: watching from a height is the oldest layer and still explains the spelling.
branches.cn: 最初的姿态：从高处观察是最古老的一层，至今仍能解释拼写。

branches.en: GUESS MADE PUBLIC: one guess is countable, and many guesses become talk about other people.
branches.cn: 被说出的猜测：一个猜测可数，许多猜测就成了对他人的议论。

branches.en: THOUGHT WITHOUT OBSERVATION: when the object cannot be seen, looking turns into reasoning.
branches.cn: 不靠观察的思考：对象看不见时，看就转为推理。

branches.en: MONEY ON A PRICE: the guess is converted into a position, in any market including land.
branches.cn: 押在价格上的钱：猜测被换成头寸，可用于任何市场，包括土地。

branches.en: A MOTIVE TO HOLD: economics names the reason for keeping cash or an asset idle.
branches.cn: 持有的动机：经济学为让现金或资产闲置给出理由。

intro.en: Speculation is a Latin noun of root plus suffix; the root means 'to look', and a tower stands between the looking and the guessing.
intro.cn: 「猜测」是词根加后缀的拉丁名词；词根意为「看」，一座塔立在「看」与「猜」之间。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere 'to look' yields specula, speculari and speculatio, and the same root reaches English in inspect, spectacle and perspective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 specere「看」衍生出瞭望塔、观察与猜测，同一词根还以检查、景象与透视进入英语。

items.exampleCN: 这个动词给单纯的看见加上目的。

items.example: The word entered English in the fourteenth century.

items.example: The parade was a fine spectacle.

items.exampleCN: 这座小山提供了俯瞰山谷的视角。
